tab_application.tex.what: The five estimators on the NHANES application, with cluster-bootstrap standard errors and intervals, the recovered measurement-error moments, the two weight ratios and the two efficiency coefficients.

sources.filter: all five estimators; the ratio column is the bootstrap variance divided by that of TC-LS over the same resamples
the quantity, design and specification blocks
the TC-PMM2*:TC-LS cluster-bootstrap ratio

tab_application.tex.aggregation: none; every entry is an evidence row. Intervals are percentile intervals of the stratified cluster bootstrap; the variance-ratio interval is a delete-one-stratum jackknife, because with 15 strata the ratio itself is the poorly determined quantity.

tab_bias.tex.what: Bias of the slope estimator, contrasting the two uncorrected estimators (naive LS, naive PMM2) with the corrected ones; the naive-PMM2 column shows that PMM2 on its own makes the EIV bias worse rather than better.

sources.filter: param='b1'; n=1000; b1_true=+1; delta=0; u_family in {gamma_wh,gamma_fixed}; lam in {0.80,0.90,0.95}; eps_key in {gauss,g_c3_0.5,g_c3_1.0,g_c3_1.5}; estimator in ['naive_ls', 'naive_pmm2', 'tc_ls', 'tc_pmm2_oracle', 'tc_pmm2star_oracle', 'tc_pmm2star_adaptive']

tab_bias.tex.aggregation: none for the estimator columns; values are rounded to four decimals, which is finer than the Monte Carlo standard error of any entry. The "attenuation" column is the textbook -(1-lambda)*beta_1 evaluated at the row's own lam and b1_true from the same evidence rows; the closing line is the largest se_bias over every cell and estimator in the table.
tab_bias.tex.labels: column U: 'W&H' = gamma of shape 4(1-lambda)/lambda, scale 1/2 (Woolsey-Huang design); 'k=4' = gamma of fixed shape 4 with the scale set by nu_2. Row c_3(eps) = 0 is the Gaussian control, where eps ~ N(0,1) rather than a centred gamma. The wrapping caption should spell both of these out.

tab_coverage.tex.what: Empirical coverage of the nominal 95% sandwich confidence interval for the slope, by estimator, with naive LS as the contrast.

sources.filter: param='b1'; delta=0; n >= 500; u_family in {gamma_wh,gamma_fixed} -- exactly the selection gate G4 applies; estimator in ['tc_ls', 'tc_pmm2_oracle', 'tc_pmm2_adaptive', 'tc_pmm2star_oracle', 'tc_pmm2star_adaptive', 'naive_ls']

tab_coverage.tex.aggregation: min / mean / max of the per-cell coverage over the 96 qualifying cells, plus the largest per-cell Monte Carlo standard error of a coverage rate. Gate G4 requires every cell in [93, 97]%.

tab_gates.tex.what: The pre-registered verification gates with their status and the number of sub-checks passed.

columns: the [PASS]/[FAIL] gate headings and the closing summary block
sources.filter: all gates in the order printed by scripts/verify.py: G0, G0b, C1, G1, G2, G2b, G3, G4, G5, G6

tab_gates.tex.aggregation: the report is parsed, not re-derived: gate names, statuses, descriptions and x/y sub-check counts are taken verbatim from the machine-written report, so the table cannot drift from the run that produced it.

tab_lambda_star.tex.what: Break-even reliability lambda* at which the fixed-weight TC-PMM2 stops losing to TC-LS: Monte Carlo estimate against the closed form. TC-PMM2* has no break-even (ARE* <= 1 for every lambda).

sources.filter: estimator_a='tc_pmm2_oracle'; estimator_b='tc_ls'; param='b1'; delta=0; eps_key != 'gauss' (ARE is identically 1 there, so no crossing exists); n=1000; lam grid [0.86, 0.88, 0.9, 0.92, 0.94, 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98]
joined on (eps_key, u_family, b1); blank means the closed-form ARE never crosses 1

tab_lambda_star.tex.aggregation: lambda* is obtained by linear interpolation between the two adjacent grid reliabilities whose measured RE brackets 1 -- byte-for-byte the rule used by scripts/verify.py, so the table reproduces the verification report.

tab_lognormal.tex.what: The numbers behind fig6: convergence, bias, MSE and MSE ratio against TC-LS for both estimators in oracle and adaptive form under lognormal measurement error, with the gate G6 counts.

sources.filter: u_family='lognormal'; param='b1'; delta=0; table body: eps_key='g_c3_1.0', n=1000, lam in {0.80,0.90,0.95}, b1_true in {+1,-1}; G6 footer: all 36 lognormal cells (both eps_key, n in {250,500,1000}, both b1_true)
same body cells; estimator_b='tc_ls'
used only as an assertion target -- see aggregation

tab_lognormal.tex.aggregation: Body rows are copied verbatim, one per cell and estimator. The G6 footer re-applies the gate rule of scripts/verify.py (defined = convergence >= 99% and finite bias; unbiased = |bias| <= max(0.25|bias of naive PMM2|, 2 SE)) and splits it per estimator into G6a "defined" and G6b "defined and unbiased". The script asserts that the two oracle variants reproduce the 52/72 recorded in verification_report.txt, so the split cannot drift from the gate it decomposes.
tab_lognormal.tex.note: eps_key=g_c3_1.5 behaves materially the same and is omitted from the body for width; it is included in the G6 footer counts. The ARE column for the fixed-weight rows is far above the measured ratio (104.47 against 13.720 at lam=0.80) because an estimator that fails to converge in part of the sample is not described by its own asymptotics; the G2 gate never covered this design.

tab_main_re.tex.what: Measured relative efficiency against TC-LS with its Monte Carlo standard error, next to the closed-form ARE, for both the transplanted-weight TC-PMM2 and TC-PMM2*.

sources.filter: param='b1'; n=1000; delta=0; estimator_b='tc_ls'; estimator_a in {tc_pmm2_oracle,tc_pmm2star_oracle}; eps_key in {g_c3_0.5,g_c3_1.0,g_c3_1.5}; u_family in {gamma_wh,gamma_fixed}; b1_true in {+1,-1}; lam in {0.80,0.90,0.95}
same cells, estimator='tc_ls', param='b1'

tab_main_re.tex.aggregation: none; one row per cell, values copied verbatim. RE values above 1 (TC-PMM2 worse than TC-LS) are set in bold.

fig1_are_theory_vs_mc.pdf.note: The systematic offset of the TC-PMM2* markers above their curve in the b1=-1 panels is the finite-sample deviation recorded by gate G2 (11/144 sub-checks outside 2 SE, |z| <= 3.14, 5 of them at n=250 and 2 at n=1000; evidence/confirmatory/verification_report.txt). It is not a plotting artefact and no smoothing is applied.
